
```{r rmats-concordance, eval=(have_rmats && rmats_conc_ok), fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
# A specificity check on the section's own primary result. Points off the
# diagonal are events where the exon-body reads disagree with the junction
# reads, which are the ones to distrust. Colouring by event type lets the RI
# cluster, if there is one, become visible without being asserted.
conc <- rmats %>%
  select(contrast, event_key, event_type, event_label, gene,
         count_mode, IncLevelDifference) %>%
  filter(!is.na(IncLevelDifference)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = count_mode, values_from = IncLevelDifference) %>%
  filter(!is.na(JC), !is.na(JCEC))

p <- ggplot(conc, aes(JC, JCEC, colour = event_type,
                      text = paste0(gene,
                                    "<br>", event_label,
                                    "<br>JC: ", round(JC, 3),
                                    "<br>JCEC: ", round(JCEC, 3)))) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "#868e96", linetype = "dashed",
              linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(size = 0.9, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ contrast, ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("SE" = "#c2255c", "MXE" = "#1c7ed6",
                                 "A3SS" = "#0ca678", "A5SS" = "#f08c00",
                                 "RI" = "#7048e8"), drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "PSI difference, junction counts only",
       y = "PSI difference, junction and exon counts", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
```

```{r rmats-h-table, eval=have_rmats, results="asis"}
cat("\n## Results table\n")
```

```{r rmats-table, eval=(have_rmats && rmats_ok)}
# One table for all five event types, with Event as a filterable column, rather
# than five subsections. The coordinates are deliberately left out: they differ
# per event type, which is what would force the split, and anyone following up a
# specific event needs the result file itself.
tbl <- rmats_jc %>%
  filter(significant) %>%
  arrange(FDR, desc(abs(IncLevelDifference))) %>%
  transmute(Contrast = contrast, Gene = gene, `Gene ID` = GeneID,
            Event = event_type, `Event ID` = ID,
            `PSI 1` = round(psi_1, 3), `PSI 2` = round(psi_2, 3),
            `PSI difference` = round(IncLevelDifference, 3),
            `Reads 1` = reads_1, `Reads 2` = reads_2,
            PValue, FDR)
truncated <- nrow(tbl) > MAX_TABLE_ROWS
if (truncated) tbl <- head(tbl, MAX_TABLE_ROWS)
cap <- if (truncated) {
  sprintf("Top %d significant events by FDR (of %d).", MAX_TABLE_ROWS,
          sum(rmats_jc$significant))
} else {
  sprintf(paste("All %d significant JC events (FDR &lt; %.2f, |PSI difference|",
                "&gt; %g). Groups 1 and 2 are the first and second condition in",
                "the contrast name; reads are the junction totals behind each",
                "group's estimate."),
          nrow(tbl), PSI_FDR_CUT, DPSI_CUT)
}
dt <- DT::datatable(tbl, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top", caption = cap,
                    options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE))
DT::formatSignif(dt, c("PValue", "FDR"), digits = 3)
```

```{r rmats-h-overlap, eval=have_rmats, results="asis"}
cat("\n## Splicing without expression change\n")
```

```{r rmats-de-overlap-note, eval=(have_rmats && rmats_ok && !(have_deseq2 || have_edger)), results="asis"}
cat("\n*This comparison needs gene-level differential expression results.*\n")
```

```{r rmats-de-overlap, eval=(have_rmats && rmats_ok && (have_deseq2 || have_edger))}
# The most useful line in the section. A gene whose splicing changed but whose
# total expression did not is regulated at isoform level, and it is invisible
# everywhere else in this report: the DE tables miss it by construction and the
# enrichment sections read from the DESeq2 ranked list, so it never reaches
# them either.
#
# Matched on gene identifier alone. rMATS reports the GeneID from the GTF, which
# is the same identifier the count matrix is built on, but a version suffix or a
# symbol-based annotation would break the join silently, so the join size is
# reported rather than assumed.
de_ref <- if (have_deseq2) {
  deseq2 %>% transmute(contrast, gene_id, de_sig = significant)
} else {
  edger %>% transmute(contrast, gene_id, de_sig = significant)
}
de_name <- if (have_deseq2) "DESeq2" else "edgeR"

spl <- rmats_jc %>%
  filter(significant) %>%
  distinct(contrast, gene_id = GeneID)

# rMATS quotes gene ids from the GTF, which for Ensembl carry a version suffix
# the count matrix may not have. Strip it on both sides before matching.
strip_ver <- function(x) sub("\\.[0-9]+$", "", x)
spl$gene_id    <- strip_ver(spl$gene_id)
de_ref$gene_id <- strip_ver(de_ref$gene_id)

j <- spl %>% left_join(de_ref, by = c("contrast", "gene_id"))

tbl <- j %>%
  group_by(Contrast = contrast) %>%
  summarise(`Genes with splicing change` = n(),
            `Also differentially expressed` = sum(de_sig %in% TRUE),
            `Splicing only` = sum(!(de_sig %in% TRUE) & !is.na(de_sig)),
            `Not in the DE table` = sum(is.na(de_sig)),
            .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(tbl, caption = sprintf(paste(
  "Genes carrying a significant JC splicing event, against the %s calls for the",
  "same contrast. 'Splicing only' genes were tested for expression and did not",
  "change: they are regulated at isoform level and appear nowhere else in this",
  "report. 'Not in the DE table' means the gene identifier did not match, which",
  "is a filtering or annotation difference rather than a result."), de_name))
```

# Functional enrichment

```{r enrich-note, results="asis"}
if (!have_gsea && !have_gprofiler) {
  cat("\n*No functional-enrichment results were produced. GSEA needs `--gmt`;",
      "both GSEA and gProfiler are skipped by `--stop_at preQC/postQC/DE`.*\n")
}
```

## GSEA

GSEA (fgsea) is run on the whole ranked DESeq2 gene list, so it captures
coordinated shifts a hard cutoff would miss. A positive NES means the gene set
is enriched in the first condition of the contrast.

```{r gsea-note, results="asis"}
if (!have_gsea) cat("\n*No GSEA results were produced (no `--gmt` supplied).*\n")
```

```{r gsea-load, eval=have_gsea, include=FALSE}
gsea <- bind_rows(lapply(gsea_files, function(f) {
  d <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  d$X <- NULL   # older results carried an unnamed index column
  d$contrast <- sub("\\.csv$", "", sub("gsea_stats_", "", basename(f)))
  d
}))
keep <- intersect(c("contrast", "pathway", "NES", "ES", "pval", "padj", "size"),
                  names(gsea))
gsea <- gsea[, keep, drop = FALSE]
if ("NES" %in% names(gsea)) gsea$NES <- round(gsea$NES, 3)
if ("ES"  %in% names(gsea)) gsea$ES  <- round(gsea$ES, 3)
gsea <- gsea[order(gsea$padj), ]
# fgsea sets NES/padj to NA for pathways whose p-value could not be estimated,
# so the plot needs both present.
gsea_ok <- nrow(gsea) > 0 && all(c("NES", "padj", "pathway") %in% names(gsea)) &&
           any(!is.na(gsea$NES) & !is.na(gsea$padj))
```

### Top enriched gene sets

The `gsea_plot_*` figures in `gsea_output/` are fgsea's own table-with-sparklines
layout, which has no interactive equivalent. This is the readable substitute:
the most significant gene sets per contrast, ordered by enrichment score. A
positive NES means the set is enriched in the first condition of the contrast.

```{r gsea-dotplot, eval=(have_gsea && gsea_ok), fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
MAX_GSEA_SETS <- 20   # per contrast, by adjusted p-value

gs <- gsea %>%
  filter(!is.na(NES), !is.na(padj)) %>%
  group_by(contrast) %>%
  slice_min(padj, n = MAX_GSEA_SETS, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    # Long MSigDB / GO names dominate the panel otherwise.
    label = ifelse(nchar(pathway) > 55, paste0(substr(pathway, 1, 52), "..."),
                   pathway),
    label = factor(label, levels = unique(label[order(NES)])),
    text  = paste0(pathway,
                   "<br>NES: ", round(NES, 3),
                   "<br>padj: ", signif(padj, 3),
                   if ("size" %in% names(gsea)) paste0("<br>genes: ", size) else ""))

p <- ggplot(gs, aes(NES, label, colour = padj, text = text)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#868e96", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(size = if ("size" %in% names(gs)) size else 3)) +
  facet_wrap(~ contrast, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_gradient(low = "#c2255c", high = "#ced4da", name = "padj") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 6), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "normalised enrichment score (NES)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
```

```{r gsea-dotplot-note, eval=(have_gsea && !gsea_ok), results="asis"}
cat("\n*No gene sets with an estimable enrichment score were returned,",
    "so the summary plot is omitted.*\n")
```

### Results table

```{r gsea-table, eval=have_gsea}
dt <- DT::datatable(gsea, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
        caption = "fgsea results across all contrasts.",
        options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE))
DT::formatSignif(dt, intersect(c("pval", "padj"), names(gsea)), digits = 3)
```

```{r gsea-plots, eval=have_gsea, out.width="80%"}

gplots <- list.files(gsea_dir, "^gsea_plot_.*\\.svg$", full.names = TRUE)
pngs   <- list.files(gsea_dir, "^gsea_plot_.*\\.png$", full.names = TRUE)
gplots <- c(gplots, pngs[!sub("\\.png$", "", pngs) %in% sub("\\.svg$", "", gplots)])
if (length(gplots)) knitr::include_graphics(sort(gplots))
```

## gProfiler

gProfiler tests the thresholded significant gene lists for over-represented GO
terms and pathways, separately for the up- and down-regulated genes.

```{r gprofiler-note, results="asis"}
if (!have_gprofiler) cat("\n*No gProfiler results were produced in this run.*\n")
```

```{r gprofiler-load, eval=have_gprofiler, include=FALSE}
wanted <- c("contrast", "direction", "source", "term_id", "term_name",
            "p_value", "term_size", "intersection_size")
gpr <- bind_rows(lapply(gprofiler_files, function(f) {
  d <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  base <- sub("\\.csv$", "", sub("^gprofiler_", "", basename(f)))
  d$direction <- sub("_.*$", "", base)
  d$contrast  <- sub("^(UP|DOWN)_", "", base)
  d[, intersect(wanted, names(d)), drop = FALSE]
}))
# The CSV is written with every column as character, so the numeric ones have
# to be restored before anything can be plotted or sorted by them.
for (nm in intersect(c("p_value", "term_size", "intersection_size"), names(gpr)))
  gpr[[nm]] <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gpr[[nm]]))
if ("p_value" %in% names(gpr)) gpr <- gpr[order(gpr$p_value), ]
gpr_ok <- nrow(gpr) > 0 && "p_value" %in% names(gpr)
```

### Enriched terms

Each point is an enriched term, arranged by source and coloured by it, with the
strongest enrichments highest. Hover for the term name, its identifier, and how
many of your genes it captured. This is the interactive counterpart of the
`gostplot_*` Manhattan plots written to `gprofiler_output/`.

```{r gprofiler-plot, eval=(have_gprofiler && gpr_ok), fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
# Laid out like gProfiler's own Manhattan plot: terms grouped along x by source,
# -log10 p up the y axis. The x position is a rank within each panel rather than
# anything meaningful, which is true of gostplot as well -- it exists to spread
# the terms out, so the axis is left unlabelled.
gp <- gpr %>%
  filter(!is.na(p_value)) %>%
  arrange(contrast, direction, source, p_value) %>%
  group_by(contrast, direction) %>%
  mutate(x = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    neglog10p = -log10(pmax(p_value, 1e-300)),
    # A plain hyphen, not an entity: this is a facet label drawn inside the
    # plot as text, so "&mdash;" would appear literally rather than resolving.
    panel     = paste0(contrast, " - ", direction),
    text      = paste0(term_name, " (", term_id, ")",
                       "<br>source: ", source,
                       "<br>p: ", signif(p_value, 3),
                       "<br>genes: ", intersection_size, " of ", term_size))

p <- ggplot(gp, aes(x, neglog10p, colour = source, text = text)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = intersection_size), alpha = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 6), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "-log10 p-value", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
```

```{r gprofiler-plot-note, eval=(have_gprofiler && !gpr_ok), results="asis"}
cat("\n*gProfiler returned no terms to plot for this run.*\n")
```

```{r gprofiler-table, eval=have_gprofiler}
dt <- DT::datatable(gpr_tbl, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
        caption = "gProfiler over-representation of the up/down gene lists.",
        options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE))

dt
```

# Files and locations

```{r files-intro, results="asis"}
cat("Where this run wrote everything, relative to its results directory.",
    "The links resolve while this document sits in `quarto_report/` alongside",
    "the other output folders; if it has been sent on by itself they will not,",
    "so every location is given as text as well.\n")
```

```{r files-table, results="asis"}
# An index of where this run wrote its outputs, built from the route the run
# actually took: a pseudo-aligner has no BAMs to index or coverage to plot, a
# --counts run has no reads to QC, and optional analyses appear only when they
# were requested.
#
# These are locations, not a presence check. The report is given only its own
# inputs, so it cannot see most of these directories -- listing a path is
# useful regardless, and a directory that is missing is informative in itself.
aligner   <- mf("analysis", "aligner")
bam_route <- !is.na(aligner) && aligner %in% c("star", "hisat2")
tx_route  <- !is.na(aligner) && aligner %in% c("salmon", "kallisto")
optional  <- unlist(manifest$analysis$optional)

frow <- function(group, name, desc, path) {
  data.frame(group = group, name = name, desc = desc, path = path,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

items <- list()
add <- function(...) items[[length(items) + 1]] <<- frow(...)

if (have_deseq2) {
  add("Differential expression", "DESeq2",
      "Result tables per contrast, figures, and a reproduce/ folder that redraws them",
      "deseq2_output/")
}
if (have_edger) {
  add("Differential expression", "edgeR",
      "Result tables per contrast, figures, and a reproduce/ folder", "edger_output/")
}
if (have_gsea) {
  add("Functional enrichment", "GSEA",
      "Enrichment statistics, ranks, and the gene-set plots", "gsea_output/")
}
if (have_gprofiler) {
  add("Functional enrichment", "gProfiler",
      "Over-representation of the up and down gene lists", "gprofiler_output/")
}

if (bam_route) {
  add("Quantification", "featureCounts",
      "Gene-level count matrix and per-sample assignment summaries", "featurecounts/")
} else if (tx_route) {
  add("Quantification", "tximport",
      "Transcript quantification summarised to gene level, and the txi object",
      "tximport/")
}

add("Quality control", "MultiQC",
    "The authoritative per-sample QC report, across every tool that ran",
    paste0("multiqc/", mqc_report_name))
if (!identical(mf("analysis", "entry"), "count matrix")) {
  add("Quality control", "FastQC", "Per-sample raw read quality", "fastqc/")
  add("Quality control", "fastp", "Adapter and quality trimming reports", "fastp/")
}
if (bam_route) {
  add("Quality control", "RSeQC",
      "Strandedness inference, read distribution and gene-body coverage", "rseqc/")
}

if (!is.na(aligner)) {
  add("Alignment and quantification", toupper(aligner),
      if (bam_route) "Sorted BAM files, their indexes and alignment logs"
      else "Per-sample quantification directories",
      paste0(aligner, "/"))
}
if (bam_route) {
  add("Alignment and quantification", "Coverage tracks",
      "BigWig tracks for a genome browser", "bam_to_bigwig/")
}

for (o in optional) {
  d <- if (grepl("splicing", o))        "diffsplice_output/"
       else if (grepl("transcript usage", o)) "dtu_output/"
       else if (grepl("isoform", o))    "isoform_switch_output/"
       else if (grepl("fusion", o))     "star_fusion/"
       else NA_character_
  if (!is.na(d)) add("Optional analyses", o, "Requested for this run", d)
}
if (have_rmats) {
  # No longer hedged with "when the run included it": rmats_output/ is staged
  # into this report now, so its presence is known rather than guessed.
  # No glob characters in the description: this chunk's output is parsed as
  # markdown before it reaches the page, so a leading asterisk is taken as an
  # emphasis marker and silently deleted. "*.MATS.JC.txt" rendered as
  # ".MATS.JC.txt", which is a filename that does not exist.
  add("Optional analyses", "rMATS",
      paste("Alternative splicing events, one subdirectory per contrast.",
            "The MATS.JC.txt and MATS.JCEC.txt files hold the results;",
            "everything else there is an rMATS intermediate"),
      "rmats_output/")
}

add("Provenance", "Run manifest",
    "How this run was configured, machine-readable; the source of section 2",
    "pipeline_info/run_manifest.json")
add("Provenance", "Run summary",
    "Duration, per-process resource use and completion status, written after this report",
    "pipeline_info/run_summary.html")
add("Provenance", "Software versions",
    "Every tool and version collected at run time", "pipeline_info/software_versions_mqc.yml")
add("Provenance", "Execution trace",
    "Nextflow's own timeline, report and trace files", "pipeline_info/")

tbl <- do.call(rbind, items)

out <- character(0)
for (g in unique(tbl$group)) {
  out <- c(out, paste0("<tr class='rf-group'><th colspan='3'>", esc(g), "</th></tr>"))
  part <- tbl[tbl$group == g, ]
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(part))) {
    r <- part[i, ]
    out <- c(out, paste0(
      "<tr><td><strong>", esc(r$name), "</strong></td>",
      "<td>", esc(r$desc), "</td>",
      "<td><a href='../", r$path, "'><code>", esc(r$path), "</code></a></td></tr>"))
  }
}

cat("<table class='rf-filetable'>",
    "<thead><tr><th>Output</th><th>Contents</th><th>Location</th></tr></thead><tbody>",
    paste(out, collapse = ""), "</tbody></table>\n", sep = "")
```
